completion_promises.criterion_text: Module imports successfully when graphiti-core is uninstalled (verified by integration test that runs in a venv without graphiti-core)
completion_promises.evidence: graphiti_core import lives only inside _load_graphiti_core() (function body) — no top-level import. test_module_top_level_has_no_graphiti_core_import scans the source and fails on any top-level graphiti import. test_module_loads_in_subprocess_with_graphiti_core_absent launches a fresh python -c subprocess that pre-sets sys.modules['graphiti_core']=None (which causes any subsequent `import graphiti_core` to raise ImportError) and confirms study_tutor.knowledge.graphiti_client still imports cleanly and GraphitiConnectionConfig is constructible. Both pass.

completion_promises.criterion_text: get_client() returns None (not raises) when graphiti-core is absent, FalkorDB is unreachable, or healthcheck times out
completion_promises.evidence: get_client() implements the three documented degradation gates: (1) ImportError from _load_graphiti_core → log + return None; (2) any exception from FalkorDriver(...) or Graphiti(...) construction → log + return None; (3) healthcheck() returning False (timeout or driver exception) → log + close partial wrapper + return None. No exception escapes. Verified by test_get_client_returns_none_when_graphiti_core_import_fails (patches _load_graphiti_core to raise ImportError), test_get_client_returns_none_when_driver_construction_fails (driver_cls side_effect=ConnectionRefusedError), and test_get_client_returns_none_when_healthcheck_times_out (slow driver + 0.05s timeout). All three assert result is None and pass.

completion_promises.criterion_text: GraphitiConnectionConfig rejects invalid values (negative port, non-positive timeout)
completion_promises.evidence: GraphitiConnectionConfig uses pydantic Field constraints: falkor_port=Field(gt=0) (rejects 0 and negatives), timeout_seconds=Field(default=5.0, gt=0) (rejects 0 and negatives). model_config=ConfigDict(extra='forbid') rejects unknown fields. Verified by test_config_rejects_negative_port, test_config_rejects_zero_port, test_config_rejects_zero_timeout, test_config_rejects_negative_timeout, and test_config_rejects_extra_fields — all pass.

completion_promises.criterion_text: healthcheck() honours timeout_seconds (5s default per ASSUM-005)
completion_promises.evidence: GraphitiClient.healthcheck wraps the inner _ping() in asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=self._config.timeout_seconds). Default timeout_seconds=5.0 matches ASSUM-005. Verified by test_config_default_timeout_matches_assum_005 (cfg.timeout_seconds == 5.0), test_healthcheck_respects_short_timeout (slow driver sleeping 0.5s with timeout_seconds=0.05 returns False well under 0.3s), and test_get_client_returns_none_when_healthcheck_times_out (covers the get_client() integration path).

completion_promises.criterion_text: Structured log line on every degradation path: event=graphiti_client_degraded with error_class, falkor_host, degraded=true
completion_promises.evidence: All degradation paths funnel through _log_degraded(error_class, host, *, latency_ms=None, error_message=None) which calls logger.warning with extra={event: 'graphiti_client_degraded', error_class, falkor_host, degraded: True, latency_ms?, error_message?}. EVENT_DEGRADED is a module constant. Tests assert these LogRecord attributes via getattr(rec, 'event', None) == mod.EVENT_DEGRADED, rec.error_class, rec.falkor_host, rec.degraded is True. Covered by test_get_client_returns_none_when_graphiti_core_import_fails, test_get_client_returns_none_when_driver_construction_fails, test_get_client_returns_none_when_healthcheck_times_out, and test_healthcheck_returns_false_when_driver_raises.

completion_promises.criterion_text: close() is idempotent and safe to call when client is None
completion_promises.evidence: GraphitiClient.close() short-circuits when self._inner is None. On the first real close it captures the inner reference, sets self._inner = None *before* awaiting (re-entrancy / concurrent-close safety), then calls inner.close() inside try/except so a raising shutdown cannot propagate. Verified by test_close_is_safe_when_inner_is_none (None inner, two close() calls, no exception), test_close_calls_inner_close_exactly_once_then_zeros_state (asserts inner.close.assert_awaited_once() across two close() calls and client_or_none is None), and test_close_swallows_inner_close_exceptions.
